title: M6: Bridge record_use endpoint + surface caps
description: Expose metering through the sidecar so non-Rust clients can consume usage. Add POST /v1/record-use (bearer plus rate-limited) and include usage (current/max) in ValidationResponse.

title: M5: Implement UsageRemaining FSE selector from local usage
description: UsageRemaining (model.rs:26) currently always returns Missing. Wire it to the actual remaining uses (maxUses - current local uses) when the meter feature is on, so FSE rules can express usage caps. When feature off or no cap, returns Missing (preserving current contract).
acceptance_criteria: With meter on and a cap set, GatewardenEvalInput populates UsageRemaining = U64(maxUses - local_uses). A rule Predicate::MinU64(remaining) evaluates correctly in FSE engine tests. Without meter, UsageRemaining stays Missing and existing behavior holds. Add FSE compliance test.

title: M4: Wire local count into check_access_with_usage
description: Replace the additional_uses: 0 no-op at manager.rs:202 so the per-license local usage count is passed into the cap check. Today caps.allows_usage(0) is always true unless Keygen already reports over-limit; with this, local enforcement actually fires.
acceptance_criteria: enforce_policy passes meter.monthly_count(clock) (or 0 when feature off) as additional_uses. A license at local count == maxUses returns UsageLimitExceeded from check_access and validate_key. Tests cover at-limit and over-limit boundaries. Default (no meter) behavior unchanged.

title: M3: Add LicenseManager::record_use entry point
description: Add public LicenseManager::record_use(key) that drives metering: increments the local meter for a license key, persists to disk, and re-checks the usage cap (local count plus Keygen maxUses), returning UsageLimitExceeded when exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: manager.record_use(key) increments meter by 1 (verified via meter.monthly_count), persists to disk, and returns Err(UsageLimitExceeded) when local+1 would exceed maxUses. Unit test with MockClock proves rollover-aware increment and persistence reload. Cfg-gated so default build lacks the method.

title: M2: Add GatewardenError::MeterIO variant (gated)

acceptance_criteria: With --features meter, GatewardenError::MeterIO(String) exists and is constructed by meter persistence failures. Without the feature the variant is absent and cargo build (default) succeeds. cargo test (default) and cargo test --features meter both green. title: 0.4.2 — Deliver offline usage metering
description:
0.4.2 — Deliver offline usage metering (THE headline feature).

WHY THIS EXISTS (history — do not repeat past mistakes):
- v0.4.0 DELIBERATELY shelved the client-side meter (src/meter/UsageMeter,
  UsageStats) as "unwired dead code". This was a CONSCIOUS decision to ship a
  clean 0.4.0, NOT a bug. See docs/shelved/usage-meter.md and CHANGELOG 0.4.0
  "Removed (breaking)".
- v0.4.1 shipped successfully (rate-limit bypass fix, sha2 dedupe, dep bumps).
- The meter is a genuinely valuable, differentiating feature: offline-enforceable
  usage caps ("500 calls/month, enforced locally even when offline") that the
  server-side Keygen maxUses cannot guarantee without connectivity.
- 0.4.2 revives it PROPERLY: wired into the public API AND the enforcement path,
  not a sealed island.

DESIGN (agreed):
- Feature-gated behind a new cargo feature `meter` so the default build is
  unchanged (non-breaking, additive API).
- Per-license-keyed meter (NEW design in the working tree — keyed by license-key
  hash; each license enforces its own maxUses locally/offline). This supersedes
  the original per-namespace design from b6c49071c8579ea477b309c016cfb68e33d501bb.
- Public entry point: LicenseManager::record_use(key).
- Thread local count into check_access_with_usage (replacing the
  additional_uses:0 no-op at manager.rs:202).
- Restore GatewardenError::MeterIO (gated).
- Wire UsageRemaining FSE selector (M5); bridge /v1/record-use endpoint + surface
  caps (M6); CI feature gate (M7); CHANGELOG/docs (M8).

CRITICAL WORKING-TREE STATE (read before touching any meter code):
- A PARTIAL, UNCOMMITTED, UNWIRED per-license meter implementation already exists
  in the working tree: src/meter/{mod,usage}.rs (new per-license design,
  cfg(feature=meter)) and a `meter = []` feature in Cargo.toml.
- It is NOT yet wired: src/lib.rs has no `pub mod meter;` (gated), manager.rs has
  no record_use, MeterIO is not restored. It will NOT compile as-is (orphaned).
- THIS IS THE IN-PROGRESS REVIVAL — DO NOT DELETE IT AGAIN. Adopt and wire it via
  M1–M4 rather than recovering the old per-namespace version from b6c49071.

See also: docs/shelved/usage-meter.md (recovery instructions for the original
design), gatewarden-sessions-combined.md (full session transcript of the meter
saga and how context was lost before), and tasks M1–M8 below.

Mark it as not-planned or security-cautioned, or reframe as explicit opt-in with spoofing warnings. State the safe default (loopback-only, never trust forwarded IPs).

acceptance_criteria: UsageCaps exposes max_uses: Option<u64> and current_uses; all internal references updated; tests updated; doc no longer asserts a monthly period. clippy clean.

title: S7: Document UsageRemaining as not-yet-wired
description: UsageRemaining returns Missing forever. 0.4.2 implements it (M5) but until then the contract should be explicit. For 0.4.2 document that UsageRemaining is not-yet-wired (planned 0.4.2) rather than silently Missing.
